shortcut_name: two-level exact-difference constraint triggers bipartite-graph recognition
evidence: DeepSeek: "Since levels only 1,2, this equivalent endpoints have different values. Thus need 2-color graph bipartite." Kimi: "each edge endpoints differ by exactly 1, i.e., one is 1 and other is 2... graph must be bipartite." GLM: "This is essentially a bipartite graph problem!"
affordance_in_statement: Each sensor must be configured with a sensitivity level of either 1 or 2. A comparator functions correctly if and only if the absolute difference between the sensitivity levels of its two connected sensors is exactly 1.
removal_suggestion: This is the intrinsic structure of the task: with exactly two allowed levels and a required difference of one, every comparator is an inequality constraint, which is precisely bipartite coloring. Rewording the scenario cannot remove this recognition without changing or obscuring the core problem.
